components.note: A simplified form of 產 that keeps just its top part; the strokes no longer picture anything

example.hanzi: 这家工厂每天生产一千台电视。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng měitiān shēngchǎn yìqiān tái diànshì.
example.english: This factory produces a thousand TVs every day.
example.fact: 产 is used in compounds rather than alone: 生产 (to manufacture), 产品 (product), 财产 (property), 产生 (to arise). It also means childbirth: 产假 is maternity leave and 产妇 is a woman in labor.

components.note: 氵 (water) — waves are moving water
良 (liáng) gives the sound — close to làng

example.pinyin: Hǎi shàng de làng hěn dà.
example.english: The waves on the sea are big.
example.fact: 浪 means a wave, and from the restless sea came the sense "roaming" or "unrestrained": 流浪 (to wander), 浪费 (to waste). In slang, 浪 means to go out and have wild fun: 出去浪.

components.note: 不 (not) — the upper part
正 (straight) — "not straight" gives crooked

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng de huà guà wāi le.
example.english: The picture on the wall is hung crooked.
example.fact: 歪 is often a result complement: 写歪了 (written crooked), 坐歪了. Figuratively, 歪理 is twisted reasoning and 歪主意 is a bad idea. The idiom 歪打正着 means getting the right result by a lucky accident.

components.note: 欠 (yawn) — a yawning mouth suggests tiredness and rest
曷 (hé) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Lèi le jiù xiē yíhuìr ba.
example.english: If you are tired, take a little rest.
example.fact: 歇 is a colloquial, mostly northern word for taking a break: 歇一歇, 歇脚 (to stop and rest the feet). 歇业 means a shop closes, and 歇后语 is a two-part folk saying where the punch line is left unsaid.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — panting happens through the mouth
耑 (duān) gives a rough sound hint for chuǎn

example.hanzi: 他跑得太快，喘不过气来。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de tài kuài, chuǎn bu guò qì lái.
example.english: He ran so fast that he could not catch his breath.
example.fact: 喘气 means to breathe hard or just "to catch a breath": 喘口气. 哮喘 and 气喘 refer to asthma. 喘不过气 is also used figuratively when pressure feels overwhelming.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — dressing up is done with the hands
分 (fēn) gives the sound — they share the -an/-en feel

example.hanzi: 他在戏里扮演一个老人。
example.pinyin: Tā zài xì lǐ bànyǎn yí ge lǎorén.
example.english: In the play he acts as an old man.
example.fact: 扮 appears in 扮演 (to play a role), 打扮 (to dress up, very common), 假扮 (to pose as) and 扮鬼脸 (to make faces). 打扮 describes making yourself look good, not just changing clothes.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the Buddha is an enlightened person
弗 (fú) gives the sound — the older reading was close to fú

example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén qù sìmiào bài fó.
example.english: Many people go to the temple to worship the Buddha.
example.fact: 佛 is short for 佛陀, a transliteration of "Buddha." It makes 佛教 (Buddhism), 佛像 (Buddha statue) and 佛山 (Foshan). In 仿佛 (as if) it is read fú, and the Fujian dish 佛跳墙 is named "Buddha jumps over the wall."

components.note: 小 (small) — on top, narrowing to a point
大 (big) — below, widening out; small over big shows a point

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiānbǐ de tóu hěn jiān.
example.english: The tip of this pencil is very sharp.
example.fact: 尖 describes points and sharp sounds: 尖叫 (to shriek), 笔尖 (pen nib). 耳朵尖 means having sharp hearing, and 尖子生 are the top students, the "tips" of the class.

components.note: 穴 (cave) — a nest or den is a hollow shelter
呙 (guō) gives a rough sound hint

example.hanzi: 小鸟在树上做了一个窝。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo zài shù shàng zuò le yí ge wō.
example.english: The little bird built a nest in the tree.
example.fact: 窝 is a nest or den, and also the measure word for a litter or brood: 一窝小猫. 被窝 is the cozy space under the blanket, and 窝 as a verb means to stay cooped up, 窝在家里. 酒窝 is a dimple.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — an old banner was made of cloth
童 (tóng) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Nà zhuàng lóu yǒu sānshí céng.
example.english: That building has thirty floors.
example.fact: As a measure word, 幢 counts buildings (一幢楼, 一幢房子), much like 栋 (dòng). Its older reading chuáng is for banners and for 幢幢, the sense of flickering shadows, as in 鬼影幢幢.

excludeSuggestion: Rarely used except as a measure word for buildings; 栋 is a common alternative.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the character stands for a sound
幼 (yòu) gives the sound — close to yōu

example.pinyin: Yōu, nǐ jīntiān zěnme zhème zǎo?
example.english: Oh, why are you so early today?
example.fact: 呦 is a light interjection of surprise or teasing, a variant of 哟. 呦呦 imitates a deer's call in the ancient Book of Songs; Tu Youyou (屠呦呦), the Nobel-winning malaria researcher, was named from that line.

excludeSuggestion: Mostly a variant of the interjection 哟; otherwise known mainly from the name 屠呦呦.

meanings: first of the ten Heavenly Stems

components.note: The origin of the cross-in-a-frame shape is debated; it later became linked to shells and armor

example.pinyin: Jiǎfāng hé yǐfāng yào qiān hétong.
example.english: Party A and Party B need to sign the contract.
example.fact: 甲 is the first of the Heavenly Stems (甲乙丙丁), so it means "first" or "A": 甲方 (Party A) in contracts, and 桂林山水甲天下 (Guilin's scenery is the best under heaven). Also 指甲 (fingernail) and 甲骨文 (oracle bone script).

components.note: 穴 (cave) — being cornered in a hole suggests being at the end of one's means
力 (strength) — replaces the old right half in simplified form; strength running out

example.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshíhou jiālǐ hěn qióng.
example.english: His family was very poor when he was a child.
example.fact: 穷 is the plain word for poor, and 贫穷 is the formal version. Its older sense is "to exhaust," as in 无穷无尽 (endless) and 穷尽. People use it jokingly too: 我穷死了 means "I'm totally broke."

components.note: 岂 traditionally pictured a drum used for victory music; the "how could it be" meaning is a later borrowing
几 is the lower component; it contributes only a loose sound

example.hanzi: 军队唱着凯歌回到了家乡。
example.pinyin: Jūnduì chàng zhe kǎigē huí dào le jiāxiāng.
example.english: The army returned home singing a victory song.
example.fact: 凯 is bound in 凯旋 (a triumphant return) and 凯歌 (victory song). It is also very common in foreign names: 凯特 (Kate), 凯撒 (Caesar), 凯迪拉克 (Cadillac).

excludeSuggestion: Bound character, mostly met in 凯旋/凯歌 and in transliterated names.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — coolness and cold
京 (jīng) gives a rough sound hint

example.hanzi: 天气凉了，多穿点儿衣服。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì liáng le, duō chuān diǎnr yīfu.
example.english: It has turned cool, so wear a bit more.
example.fact: 凉 is pleasantly or mildly cold, milder than 冷: 凉快 (nicely cool), 凉爽, 凉菜 (cold dishes). Tea or food that has gone cold is 凉了; the word also appears in slang 凉了 meaning "we're doomed."

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling is done by hand
曳 (yè) gives the old sound — its original reading yè survives in the literary reading of 拽

example.pinyin: Tā zhuài zhe wǒ de shǒu bú fàng.
example.english: He held on to my hand and would not let go.
example.fact: 拽 means to tug or drag. In mainland slang, 他很拽 means someone acts cool and arrogant, as if swaggering. It has two other readings: zhuāi (dialect, to throw) and yè (literary, to pull).

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — gifts and rewards once accompanied praise
兟 (shēn) gives only a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 大家都称赞他的汉语说得好。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chēngzàn tā de Hànyǔ shuō de hǎo.
example.english: Everyone praised how well he speaks Chinese.
example.fact: 赞 is to praise: 称赞, 赞成 (to agree with), 赞助 (to sponsor). On Chinese social media, 点赞 means to give a "like," and 很赞 or 太赞了 is slang for "awesome."

components.note: 皿 (dish) — a vessel holding salt; the upper part is a reduced form of 卤 (brine)

example.pinyin: Cài lǐ de yán fàng duō le.
example.english: Too much salt was put in the dish.
example.fact: 盐 is salt, one of the "daily necessities" in the idiom 柴米油盐 (firewood, rice, oil, salt), meaning everyday household life. Related: 食盐 (table salt) and 海盐 (sea salt).

components.note: 饣 (food) — fullness comes from eating
包 (bāo) gives the sound — a near match for bǎo

example.pinyin: Wǒ chī bǎo le, xièxie.
example.english: I am full, thank you.
example.fact: 饱 usually attaches to 吃 as 吃饱, "eat until full." It is the polite way to refuse more food. Also 饱满 (plump), 饱和 (saturated), and 饱眼福 (to feast one's eyes). 吃饱了撑的 teases someone with too much time.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — a cabin belongs to a ship
仓 (cāng) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.hanzi: 飞机的经济舱座位比较小。
example.pinyin: Fēijī de jīngjìcāng zuòwèi bǐjiào xiǎo.
example.english: The seats in a plane's economy class are rather small.
example.fact: 舱 started out as a ship's compartment, and now covers aircraft and spacecraft: 机舱 (cabin), 经济舱 (economy class), 商务舱 (business class), 头等舱 (first class), 太空舱 (space capsule).

components.note: 页 (head) — the neck belongs to the head and body
巠 (jīng) gives the sound; the left part is its reduced form

example.pinyin: Tā de jǐngbù yǒudiǎn tòng.
example.english: His neck hurts a bit.
example.fact: 颈 is the formal or medical word for neck; everyday speech uses 脖子. 颈椎 (cervical vertebrae) is a famous complaint of office workers, and the giraffe is 长颈鹿, "long-neck deer." In 脖颈 it takes the reading gěng.

components.note: 阝 (mound/place) — the setting of the pit
臽 (a pit) — also gives the sound

example.pinyin: Qìchē xiàn zài ní lǐ le.
example.english: The car is stuck in the mud.
example.fact: 陷 means falling or sinking into a hole: 陷入 (to fall into), 陷阱 (trap), 缺陷 (defect), 沦陷 (to fall to an enemy). 陷害 means to frame someone.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — the action is moving about
狂 (kuáng) gives a rough sound hint

example.hanzi: 周末我们去商场逛逛吧。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù shāngchǎng guàngguang ba.
example.english: Let's go stroll around the mall this weekend.
example.fact: 逛街 means strolling and window-shopping without any need to buy anything, which English cannot capture in one word. It now extends to online browsing: 逛淘宝 (browsing Taobao).

components.note: 冫 (ice) — freezing
东 (dōng) gives the sound — a near match for dòng

example.hanzi: 外面太冷了，我的手都冻僵了。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài lěng le, wǒ de shǒu dōu dòngjiāng le.
example.english: It is so cold outside that my hands are frozen stiff.
example.fact: 冻 can mean frozen water, as in 冰冻, or to feel painfully cold: 冻死我了 (I'm freezing). Also 冷冻 (frozen food), 冻结 (to freeze assets) and 果冻 (jelly).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken, colloquial word
乍 (zhà) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Nǐ zǎ hái bù huí jiā?
example.english: How come you are still not going home?
example.fact: 咋 is a northern colloquial form of 怎么: 咋办 (what to do), 咋样 (how is it). Another reading zé appears in 咋舌 (to be astonished into silence).

excludeSuggestion: Dialectal, informal equivalent of 怎么 that is not suitable for formal writing.

meanings: to go so far as to

components.note: 音 (sound) — music
儿 (person) — a person at the end; together they show a piece of music ending

example.hanzi: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
example.pinyin: Tā jìngrán wàng le zìjǐ de shēngrì.
example.english: He actually forgot his own birthday.
example.fact: 竟 expresses surprise and usually appears as 竟然. It is close to 居然, with 竟 a bit more written. Its older meaning is "to finish," kept in 终竟 and 究竟 (after all), 毕竟 (after all).

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house
示 (altar) — an altar for ancestors in the home

example.hanzi: 这个宗教有很长的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhège zōngjiào yǒu hěn cháng de lìshǐ.
example.english: This religion has a long history.
example.fact: 宗 is rooted in ancestor worship: 祖宗 (ancestors), 宗族 (clan), and then 宗教 (religion), 宗旨 (aim). As a measure word it counts cases or goods: 一宗案件, 大宗货物 (bulk goods).

components.note: 日 (sun) — sunlight does the drying
西 (xī) is a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 他把被子拿到外面晒太阳。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ bèizi ná dào wàimiàn shài tàiyáng.
example.english: He took the quilt outside to air in the sun.
example.fact: 晒太阳 (to bask in the sun) is a common wish for relaxation and health; 晒被子 means airing bedding; 晒伤 is sunburn. Online, 晒 means to show off something publicly: 晒照片, 晒工资.

components.note: 木 (tree) — the fruit stone is a tree's seed
亥 (hài) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Zhège táozi de hé hěn dà.
example.english: This peach has a very big pit.
example.fact: 核 is a fruit pit, and also a nucleus or core: 核心 (core), 核桃 (walnut), 核实 (to verify). Because of the atomic nucleus, 核 now also means nuclear: 核电站, 核武器.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a sound
乌 (wū) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zài ménkǒu wūwū de jiào.
example.english: The puppy is whimpering at the door.
example.fact: 呜呜 imitates sobbing, whimpering, or a siren or train whistle. Texters use 呜呜呜 for cute crying. 呜呼 is an old exclamation of grief, and 一命呜呼 jokingly means "to kick the bucket."

components.note: 厂 (cliff, building) — a sheltering structure, per the dictionary reading
日 (sun) — sunlight inside it
子 (child) — a child within; the dictionary reads the whole as warm, rich shelter

example.hanzi: 外面很冷，你多穿一件厚衣服。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, nǐ duō chuān yí jiàn hòu yīfu.
example.english: It is cold outside, so wear a thicker coat.
example.fact: 厚 is the opposite of 薄 (báo). It describes thickness of flat things like books or coats, and figuratively generosity: 厚道 (honest and kind), 厚礼 (a generous gift). 厚脸皮 means thick-skinned or shameless.

components.note: 王 (king, here jade) — precious stones
马 (mǎ) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.hanzi: 她手上戴着一个玛瑙手镯。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒu shàng dài zhe yí ge mǎnǎo shǒuzhuó.
example.english: She is wearing an agate bracelet.
example.fact: 玛 appears alone almost never. It forms 玛瑙 (agate) and transliterations: 玛丽 (Mary), 玛雅 (Maya), 玛莎拉蒂 (Maserati).

excludeSuggestion: Only occurs in 玛瑙 and in transliterated names.

components.note: 阝 (mound) — left-hand form for hill or place; things attach to a slope
付 (fù) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Qǐng kàn fùjiàn lǐ de zīliào.
example.english: Please look at the information in the attachment.
example.fact: 附 means to attach or be near: 附近 (nearby, very common), 附件 (email attachment), 附加 (additional), 附和 (to echo someone). 附中 is a middle school attached to a university.

components.note: 亦 (also) — the upper part of the simplified form
弓 (bow) — a bow is the shape of a curve

example.pinyin: Qiánmiàn de lù yǒu yí ge dà wān.
example.english: There is a big bend in the road ahead.
example.fact: 弯 means curved or a curve: 拐弯 / 转弯 (to turn a corner), 弯路 (a detour). 绕弯子 means to beat around the bush. Also the measure word for crescent moons: 一弯新月.

components.note: 戌 (an old weapon shape) — armed force
女 (woman) — the dictionary reads it as overpowering by force of arms

example.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī hěn yǒu wēixìn.
example.english: He has a lot of authority in the company.
example.fact: 威 is about intimidating power: 威力, 威胁 (to threaten), 威风 (imposing), 示威 (to demonstrate). It also shows in names: 威尼斯 (Venice), 威士忌 (whisky).

components.note: 戈 (spear) — poking is a spear-like action
翟 (dí) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Bié yòng shǒuzhǐ chuō wǒ.
example.english: Don't poke me with your finger.
example.fact: 戳 can be to jab, a seal or a stamp (邮戳 postmark), or fig. to expose: 戳穿谎言 (to expose a lie). Nowadays 戳中 also means "to hit a nerve," as in 戳中泪点.

components.note: 乂 — crossing strokes like threads of a weave
布 (cloth) — thinly woven cloth, which suggests "sparse"; hope is a later extension

example.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng míngtiān tiānqì hǎo.
example.english: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
example.fact: 希 is mostly found in 希望 (hope, either noun or verb) and 希腊 (Greece). The "rare" sense survives in 稀 and 希奇. 希望工程 is a well-known charity that helps poor children go to school.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — a kerchief is a piece of cloth
白 (bái) gives a rough sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒupà cā le cā yǎnlèi.
example.english: She wiped her tears with a handkerchief.
example.fact: 帕 sits in 手帕 (handkerchief) and 头帕 (headscarf). It also stands in for the pascal, the unit of pressure, and for sounds in names such as 帕金森 (Parkinson).

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — gifts and valuables
易 (yì) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Huángdì cì gěi tā yí jiàn bǎowù.
example.english: The emperor bestowed a treasure on him.
example.fact: 赐 is a gift from a superior, such as an emperor: 赏赐, 恩赐. Politely, 请多赐教 ("please favor me with your guidance") is a humble stock phrase, and 天赐良机 means a golden opportunity from heaven.

components.note: 亻 (person) — an immortal is a kind of person
山 (shān) — mountain hermits; also gives a rough sound

example.hanzi: 传说山上住着一位神仙。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō shān shàng zhù zhe yí wèi shénxiān.
example.english: Legend says an immortal lives on the mountain.
example.fact: 仙 refers to immortals in Daoist belief and is often explained as "a person living in the mountains." See 神仙 (gods and immortals), 仙女 (fairy maiden), 成仙 (to become immortal) and 仙人掌 (cactus).

components.note: 士 (scholar/soldier) — strength is a warrior's trait
丬 gives the sound — it is also seen in 状

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn zhuàng, lìqi hěn dà.
example.english: He is sturdily built and very strong.
example.fact: 壮 means strong or magnificent: 强壮, 壮观 (spectacular), 壮士 (a brave warrior), 壮胆 (to boost one's courage). 壮族 is the Zhuang people, China's largest ethnic minority.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — fog is weather and water
务 (wù) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang yǒu dà wù.
example.english: There was thick fog this morning.
example.fact: 雾 is fog: 大雾, 云雾, 喷雾 (spray). 雾霾 is smog (fog plus haze), a news staple in northern China. The idiom 雾里看花 (looking at flowers through fog) describes seeing something unclearly.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — fragrance comes from plants and flowers
分 (fēn) gives the sound — it matches exactly

example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ chōngmǎn le fēnfāng.
example.english: The garden is full of fragrance.
example.fact: 芬 means fragrance and forms 芬芳 (fragrant). It is also a typical girl's name, and it supplies the sound in 芬兰 (Finland).

components.note: 亡 (wáng) gives the sound; it also suggests searching for what is gone
月 (moon) — gazing at the moon
王 — a figure standing tall, the dictionary reads a king looking out

example.pinyin: Tā wàng zhe chuāng wài de yuèliang.
example.english: He gazes at the moon outside the window.
example.fact: 望 is to gaze into the distance, and from longing comes hope: 希望, 失望 (disappointed), 看望 (to visit someone). 望子成龙 expresses parents' hope that their son will "become a dragon," meaning succeed.

components.note: An old stemmed serving dish; the character was later borrowed for "bean"

example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang hē dòujiāng, chī bāozi.
example.english: In the morning I drink soy milk and eat steamed buns.
example.fact: 豆 first pictured a ritual stemmed dish, and the "bean" meaning came later as a borrowing. It gives 豆腐 (tofu), 豆浆 (soy milk), 红豆 (red bean). Beans are counted with 颗 or 粒.

components.note: 日 (sun) — warmth comes from sunshine
爰 (yuán) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì zhēn nuǎnhuo.
example.english: The weather is really warm today.
example.fact: 暖和 (nuǎnhuo) is the colloquial adjective for pleasantly warm. 暖气 is central heating in northern China, 温暖 is warm in an emotional sense, and 暖男 describes a considerate, caring man.

components.note: 壴 (drum) — a picture of a drum on a stand
支 (zhī) — the right part looks like a hand striking, and gives a rough sound

example.pinyin: Tā zài yuèduì lǐ dǎ gǔ.
example.english: He plays the drums in the band.
example.fact: 鼓 is a drum, and the verb extends to "stir up" or "bulge": 鼓掌 (to applaud), 鼓励 (to encourage), 鼓起勇气 (to summon courage). The measure word for a drum is 面 or 通 (for a round of beating).

components.note: 氵 (water) — a harbor is a body of water
巷 (xiàng) gives a rough sound hint

example.hanzi: 这个港口每天有很多船进出。
example.pinyin: Zhège gǎngkǒu měitiān yǒu hěn duō chuán jìnchū.
example.english: Many ships come and go in this port every day.
example.fact: 港 is a harbor: 港口, 海港. 香港 (Hong Kong) means "fragrant harbor," and 港 alone is the short name for Hong Kong: 港币 (HK dollar), 港剧, 港人.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — a building, per the dictionary reading
隶 (servant) — a household attendant; the dictionary reads a house with a helper, a comfortable home

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēntǐ jiànkāng.
example.english: I wish you good health.
example.fact: 康 on its own is formal. It builds 健康 (health), 康复 (to recover), and 小康 ("moderately well-off"), a policy phrase for a comfortable society. 康熙 is the famed Kangxi emperor.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — a riddle is put in words
迷 (mí) gives the sound — it matches exactly and means "confusing"

example.hanzi: 这个谜语太难了，我猜不出来。
example.pinyin: Zhège míyǔ tài nán le, wǒ cāi bu chū lái.
example.english: This riddle is too hard, so I cannot guess it.
example.fact: 谜 is a riddle or mystery: 谜语, 谜团 (puzzle), 千古之谜 (an age-old mystery). Guessing lantern riddles (猜灯谜) is a traditional Lantern Festival activity. A Beijing form 谜儿 reads mèir.
